_about: The review questions, one packet per chapter key. The 96 approved on 2026-10-01/02 (the trimmed September packets), renumbered to the October 2026 chapters; the 11 rows the October text overtook reworded or dropped (operator 2026-10-08); the October update's full set is kept in spec-october-full.json. Keys starting with '_' are notes, not packets. P2 (operator 2026-10-08): the approved October candidates (plan 2.3, Add + Opt) added before each packet's closing Resources / Anything-else questions, each carrying its ask in its own text, plus the Denials packet.

p2.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 2: Manual Mobility & General DME

**For:** Manual Mobility (Parth Dave, Manager)

rows.q: **Manual wheelchairs** — are the capacities, codes and coverage thresholds right? And when is the **Medline K3 Guardian 20"** billed as K0006 rather than K0003 with E2201?

rows.says: **Nebulizers:** new orders stay with Manual Mobility; refill supplies go to Resupply
**Upgrade fee waivers** — the table and diagram, including uncommon payers such as Workers' Compensation or the VA, which may pay the fee in full
**Texas-only coverage:** lift chairs through the Medicaid Waiver Program; shower chairs and tub benches through Texas Medicaid. The 3-in-1 commode can be covered by Medicare anywhere
**Walkers on an insurance order are never shipped out of state** — out of state is out of range (OOR). An **out-of-pocket** order lifts the state limit, but never the delivery radius

rows.q: **Other items** — knee walkers are out-of-pocket except through VGM Homelink, and blood pressure monitors are wrist-only. Are those right? And should **crutches (E0114)** be in the guide at all?

rows.says: **A wheelchair size change has no cutoff.** Before delivery, the CSR emails the Manual Mobility Q and the team acts on it; after delivery, it goes through Service or a swap on a pick-up ticket. (The manual used to say a change after validation meant reopening the order.)

**Your team's rows in the directory** — the Manual Mobility Q and the authorization escalation now sit on the Manual Mobility Manager's row, and the Lift Chair Coordinator is backed up by the Manual Mobility Manager. Please check each holder, backup and contact

**Very high coinsurance:** orders with a very high coinsurance — often 50% or more — may be declined, depending on the item, and the intake team decides. The manual gives no figure until you confirm one: at what coinsurance level does your team decline an order, and does it depend on the item?
**The bariatric bed (E0301)** is covered by Medicare for a patient who weighs **more than 350 lbs**, up to 600 lbs — the threshold Card 2 already quoted

rows.q: **Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 2's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p3.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 3: Respiratory & Resupply

**For:** Respiratory & Resupply (Nikunj Solanki, Manager)

rows.says: **Out-of-pocket purchases** are handled by the CSR team, who email intake, eligibility and Field Operations
**Nebulizer refill supplies** are handled by Resupply, at Medicare's allowances — and **no supply of any kind** ships more than a three-month quantity at once

**Resupply timing:** under Medicare the patient confirms within the 30 days before their supply runs out, and we ship no sooner than 10 days before. Texas Medicaid bills a month at a time, with eligibility checked before each shipment
**Quantity allowances** for trach, PAP and incontinence supplies
**Compliance requirements** — PAP usage and the follow-up visit, and the documentation for oxygen, ventilators and the low air loss mattress
**Ventilators:** after hours, dispatch the on-call RT immediately. If an MDO asks about a vent referral we can't find, check with the Respiratory & Resupply Manager first
**What we do and don't offer:** no new external or Purewick catheters, no new IPPB units; oximetry testing is available

**Your team's rows in the directory** — each resupply category (CPAP; incontinence and catheter; trach, suction and ventilator) has a named owner, backed up by the Respiratory & Resupply Manager; and the Respiratory Therapists row. Please check each holder, backup and contact

**A same-items resupply** goes to the Resupply team on the email tool's **Repeat Resupply** form, subject `[Category] [Month] Resupply: [Patient name], DOB: [date]` — for example, `CPAP March Resupply: Jane Doe, DOB: 01/02/1950`. Are the form's fields right?

**Very high coinsurance:** orders with a very high coinsurance — often 50% or more — may be declined, depending on the item, and the intake team decides. The manual gives no figure until you confirm one: at what coinsurance level does your team decline an order, and does it depend on the item?
**Oximetry:** the FAQ says we can facilitate a test, and Field Ops schedules the device's delivery and pick-up together. What is the process and the use case, and who performs and reads the test?
**After-hours dispatch is DFW only.** Do we have any ventilator patients outside DFW? If so, the after-hours chapter needs to say what happens for them
**No portable oxygen concentrators** — home units only, not even out of pocket. Was a POC ever sold out of pocket, and should we offer one?
**If the PAP trial fails** — the watch-out describes Medicare and Medicare Advantage. Should it be split by payer: Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial?

rows.q: **APAP:** an APAP bills as E0601, the CPAP code, so E0601 documentation covers either, and the **Luna G3 X APAP (G4600)**, now in the CPAP table, works as either. Is that right? When a patient switches from a fixed pressure to auto, does the provider need to send a new pressure order?
**Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 3's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p4.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 4: Sales

**For:** Sales — **Mary Carson** (Sales Manager)
**Also for:** **April Arredondo** (Sales Eligibility) — questions marked **◆**

rows.says: **Sales Eligibility:** reachable by email or direct transfer to April Arredondo; takes orders back if a patient's insurance changes after the handoff ◆
**Qualified Leads** skip PAK but still get a PPD; an evaluation over 6 months old doesn't qualify
**Lead callers:** routed to the rep in the lead notes, or the Sales Q, PAP Q or Sales MWC Q; with no lead, CSRs call the Sales Q with the caller's name and number
**The Eligibility Status** — what each status means, and the progression diagram ◆
**The Power Order Process** — is Sales' part of it right?
**The Sales process** — the eight stages to the handoff
**The one-year PPD rule:** over a year means a new order through Sales
**Member ID callbacks** and **fax numbers** — Sales 210-761-7887, main 972-572-1112

rows.q: **The PAP Q and Sales MWC Q** — what should a CSR know about how each works?

rows.says: **Your team's rows in the directory** — the Sales, PAP and MWC queues now sit on the Sales Manager's row, and the individual Sales rep rows were removed. Please check each holder, backup and contact

rows.q: **A past PMD patient who wants a new PMD.** Five years or more since the last PMD was delivered → Sales creates a new order on the existing account. Within five years → usually a Same or Similar conflict, with a possible exception when the new PMD is an **upgrade** and the provider attests to a **significant change in physical condition or mobility needs**; for now this call also goes to **Sales**. Is all of this right? Should the within-five-years call stay with Sales or go to Power, and who decides whether the provider's attestation is enough?
**Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 4's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your teams?

p5.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 5: Power Mobility

**For:** Power — **Rajdeep Thakar** (Power Manager), **Erica Thongvan** (PAK) and **Ahmed Ramadan** (Qualifications)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**

rows.says: **The Power Order Process** — the phases, their order, the two ways in from Sales, and the typical times. If appeals are also denied, the order is closed

rows.q: **Qualifications documents** — is the list complete, and is each in the right group? Always: M.E. F2F, SWO, SE, LCMP Declaration, MRx. When applicable: Addendum, PT/OT Report Concurrence, PT Rx and Report, ATP Report

rows.says: **A Qualified Lead skips PAK but still gets a PPD**, from a Qualifications team member
**ATP evaluations** are scheduled by Field Ops-Power, up to 2–3 weeks out depending on the ATP's route. Virtual evaluations are scheduled only by Erica Thongvan ◆
**An insurance rep giving a PAR decision:** the CSR records it with the reference number, confirms the letter is coming, notes the account, and emails Power intake — no transfer
**The 90-day figure** is described as the national average, with UMS faster; CSRs then give the current stage
**Medicare Advantage is primary**, not secondary
**Equipment answers:** POVs can't take ROHO cushions; POVs run about $1,200–$1,900 out of pocket; no vehicle lifts; ramps out-of-pocket only; cup holders can be added

rows.q: **Same or Similar** — a patient who surrenders a PMD may not get another for five years. Are there exceptions the guide should mention?

rows.says: **Your teams' rows in the directory** — the new Power Manager row backs up Qualifications, PAK and the PAR specialists; the Qualified Leads and Order Verification rows were folded in. Please check each holder, backup and contact — and **the Power Manager has no backup recorded: who is it?**

**Very high coinsurance:** orders with a very high coinsurance — often 50% or more — may be declined, depending on the item, and the intake team decides. The manual gives no figure until you confirm one: at what coinsurance level does your team decline an order, and does it depend on the item?

**Dual submission:** some PARs go to both traditional Medicare and the patient's Medicare Advantage plan — the notes say *dual submission*. If the MA plan denies but Medicare approves, Medicare's approval is sent to the MA plan; this can add 2 weeks or more
**The power wheelchair product guide** — the models we carry. Rajdeep: please add any active model that's missing, even a less common one

**A PT evaluation** isn't required on every order, but may be needed per insurance guidelines or the doctor's recommendation. The manual doesn't say yet: when exactly is a PT evaluation, or an ATP evaluation, needed per insurance?
**If the provider refers the patient to a PT/OT,** that's fine — but we then need a PT/OT Eval Rx for the insurance, and we can help the patient through that process

**Virtual ATP evaluations** are scheduled only by Virtual ATP Scheduling — currently Erica Thongvan, backed up by the Field Ops-Power team. Who owns virtual ATP scheduling, and how should CSRs reach it? ◆

**Standard vs complex rehab PWC**, using Medicare's groupings: standard is Group 2 with no power options; complex rehab is Group 2 with single or multiple power options, and Group 3 and up. Is this how your team uses the two terms?

rows.q: **A past PMD patient within five years of the last PMD** (4.5.1, in the Sales chapter) — usually a Same or Similar conflict, with a possible exception for an upgrade the provider attests to; for now the call goes to Sales, and 5.1 points there. Should it go to Power instead?
**Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 5's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your teams?

p6.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 6: Field Operations

**For:** Field Operations — **Parth Shah** (Manager) and **Mahesh Patel** (Supervisor)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**

rows.says: **PMD pick-up requests:** adjustable problems and faults go to Service; affordability gets the EAA or a payment plan first; patient-owned chairs aren't picked up ◆
**Bed relocation:** generally not done; possible within the Dallas, San Antonio and Hawaii areas for rental beds, at $150. Either supervisor decides, and CSRs route the call to Service

**Shipping supplies:** no sooner than 10 days before the current supply runs out, and the ship date is the date of service. Overnight shipping is possible for respiratory supplies if the patient pays the difference
**Routing:** mask fitting goes to the Field Ops Q; freight companies go to Field Ops-Power with their name and delivery city; plus the common-call rules ◆

**Facility deliveries:** equipment no earlier than two days before discharge; the facility covers equipment during a Part A SNF stay; supplies only after discharge. **A PMD never goes to a hospital, rehab facility or SNF** — but it can go to a nursing home that is the patient's permanent residence, with the patient present ◆

rows.q: **Proof of delivery** — is the list of required contents right? And when are **delivery photos** taken, and when is a **driver's license** collected?
**Patient-responsibility balances** — when must *Pat. Resp.* be collected before delivery, and when can delivery be scheduled without it?

rows.says: **Used equipment:** a limited pool, mostly PWC K0821 and K0823 and CPAP; prescription items still need a prescription

**Backorders:** Field Ops updates the patient, and gives a date only if the manufacturer has. How often is the patient re-contacted? Are substitutes offered? Can the patient cancel, and how is an out-of-pocket order refunded?
**The Purchase Capped Rental Form** is signed at delivery — CSRs check Artifacts for it before conceding a "nobody told me" call
**Upgrade fee returns:** unused, within 15 days, less a 20% restocking fee
**Oximetry:** delivery and pick-up are scheduled together

**Your team's rows in the directory** — the Field Ops queues now sit on the Field Operations Manager's row, backed up by Ozaire (MD) Hawa and Mahesh Patel, and the Field Ops-Power queue on the Field Operations — Power Supervisor's row. Please check each holder, backup and contact ◆
**Ramps** are sold out of pocket only. Is there anything about an out-of-pocket ramp order a CSR should know?

**Oxygen tanks aren't delivered to a medical facility for general stock** — a request not tied to a named patient — except rarely, after checking with the Field Operations Supervisor. What is the rare exception, and who approves it?
**Texas Medicaid delivery timing**

rows.q: **Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 6's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p7.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 7: Service

**For:** Service — **Arnav Pan** (Supervisor)

rows.says: **Who pays for a repair** — rental status and warranty decide, not time since delivery; and the categories where the usual rules don't apply (oxygen, frequent-and-substantial-servicing items, anything under warranty)

**A diagnostic visit carries a $75 out-of-pocket charge** when the patient refuses the requested photos or video of the equipment and the issue, or when one of our technicians recently found the equipment working and it is again fully functional; CSRs say so **before** booking. Is the fee $75, or $150? Are these the two conditions — or is it charged whenever no photos or video were sent? And is the visit free when the technician finds and repairs a fault?
**Loaners:** never offered unprompted; possible only while patient-owned equipment is repaired, and Service confirms
**PMD problems** come to Service — including discomfort and faults behind a pick-up request. Once a repair is arranged, the visit is scheduled through Field Ops-Power
**Warranties:** usually a year; Service requests coverage and the manufacturer decides; water damage commonly voids one
**Damaged, lost or stolen equipment:** irreparable damage means an accident or disaster, not neglect; lost or stolen needs a police report before a replacement request
**Ventilators:** the Trilogy is the only one we carry; issues go to the Service Q, and after hours the on-call RT is dispatched immediately
**Bed relocation:** either supervisor decides; if approved, Service tickets and validates it, and Field Ops schedules it
**Swap-outs:** with new documents needed, the CSR creates a pick-up ticket, notes it, and emails intake; otherwise Service creates a swap-out ticket
**Routing** — including wrong item versus expectation mismatch on resupply, and CPAP set-up

rows.q: **Chargers and batteries for non-customers** — does the caller's PMD have to be exactly a model we carry, or is a compatible charger or battery enough?

rows.says: **Turnaround** isn't quoted as a range — a few days for small issues, several weeks when a part comes from the manufacturer

rows.q: **Troubleshooting guides** — does your team have any, for power wheelchairs or other equipment? If so, please share them

rows.says: **A PMD we can no longer service** — CSRs suggest a local DME repair service; for insurance to pay, it must be enrolled with or in network for the patient's plan. The competitor referrals (Numotion, WSR, National Seating & Mobility) were removed. Should any other referral guidance replace them?
**Your team's row in the directory** — the Service Q and the old Service Escalation row now sit on the Service Supervisor's row, backed up by Parth Shah. Please check the holder, backup and contact
**A package the carrier shows as delivered but the patient never received** goes to the Service Q, which opens a lost-package claim with FedEx — no police report is needed

rows.q: **Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 7's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p9.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 9: After Hours

**For:** After-hours coverage — **Robin** (Customer Service Manager), **Parth Shah** and **Shagun Shastri**

rows.says: **The escalation chain:** RT calls go to the other RT at step 3; if no one answers, repeat from step 1; 9-1-1 first if distress develops; confirm a backup cylinder meanwhile
**Power wheelchairs:** advise business hours; if the patient is stuck, non-emergency services or 9-1-1
**Dispatch and targets:** DFW only, San Antonio for concentrators only; 0–60 minutes for ventilators, concentrators and suction

rows.q: **The on-call team** — please confirm everyone and their numbers: technicians, RTs, and the Level 1 and Level 2 backups. Who, if anyone, is Level 2?

rows.says: **Each escalation step waits 30 minutes** — including between the first call-and-text and the second. Is 30 minutes right between every step, including steps 1 and 2?

**Phone first:** an on-call RT or DME technician first tries to reach the patient and troubleshoot by phone — RTs on ventilator calls too. The CSR still dispatches a ventilator call immediately and never troubleshoots it

rows.q: **Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to after hours?

p10.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 10: Billing & Denials

**For:** Billing — **Bhoj Bhatt** (Billing Manager)

rows.says: **Hospice** covers equipment related to the terminal diagnosis; unrelated equipment can still be billed. Billing decides

rows.q: **Oxygen billing** — the conserver is included in the rental and coded **A9900**; accessories are included for all five years; UMS keeps ownership after 36 months. **Has UMS been billing the conserver as E1352?**

rows.says: **Rentals:** 13 paid months to ownership; a break over 60 days plus the rest of the rental month starts a new rental
**Resupply:** the 30-day contact and 10-day shipping windows; the ship date is the date of service
**Collecting payment:** out-of-pocket orders at the Item Master price, no sales tax unless flagged; Save Card only with permission
**Upgrade fee waivers** — rules A, B and C, uncommon payers, and checking Medicaid enrollment with Eligibility
**The EAA:** Billing processes it; usually 1–2 weeks; not available on out-of-pocket orders
**Medicaid and QMB:** QMB patients are never billed cost-sharing; Texas Medicaid as secondary can cover items Medicare never covers
**Deadlines:** timely filing — Medicare 12 months, Texas Medicaid 95 days; redeterminations within 120 days
**Cost estimates and billing scenarios**
**COB and ABNs:** only the patient can update COB; ABNs are Original Medicare only, signed before delivery
**What CSRs can and can't promise**

**A PWC billed as rent-to-own with only some months paid:** the balance may be waived rather than the chair picked up, because a return can mean the insurance expects to be refunded. Under a Medicare capped rental, paid months are normally earned — does a pick-up really mean the insurance expects them refunded?

rows.q: **Texas Medicaid CPAP** — the manual says only that Medicaid and commercial plans set their own requirements. Does Texas Medicaid purchase a CPAP after 10 months of rental? Is children's adherence 50% of nights?

rows.says: **Bariatric equipment below the weight threshold** can be provided if the patient pays the difference. Is an ABN needed for a Medicare patient?

**Pick-up write-offs:** *Waived* — a company decision; the balance is waived and the item is the patient's — or *failed pick-up*, where the balance stays on the account. How is a waived balance documented, and who tells the patient?
**Swap-outs:** when an item is swapped, is the old one picked up immediately, or does billing continue until the new order completes?
**Capped rental has no purchase option — except a complex rehab power wheelchair**, which can be billed as a purchase at delivery

**E0471 (a BiPAP with a backup rate) is a capped rental, like E0470** — Medicare has paid it as one since April 2006. The manual used to call it a continuous monthly rental, never owned. Is it billed as a capped rental?

**Oxygen servicing after month 36:** repairs and parts are never separately reimbursed, but Medicare pays one maintenance-and-servicing visit every 6 months (MS modifier) for a concentrator or transfill equipment — not tanks or liquid — starting 6 months after the rental ends; it needs a real visit, and the patient owes the 20% coinsurance. Does UMS bill these visits?
**Oxygen cylinders (E0431)** are the portable add-on in the 36-month oxygen rental, not the 13-month capped rental where 10.2.1 listed them. Is that how they're billed?

**Billing order for dual eligibles:** Medicare first, then Medicaid — except a hospital bed for a full-Medicaid patient in an enrolled state, where Medicaid is primary (Rule B). Another section used to say Medicare is always billed first — which is right?
**The upgrade fee amounts** in 10.15 — do they match the Upgrade Fee (Mobility) sheet?

**A PMD within 5 years of the last:** usually a Same or Similar conflict, with a possible exception when the new PMD is an upgrade and the provider attests to a significant change in condition. Does Billing treat this as a Same or Similar exception, or as a different item?

**The oxygen restart example**, recalculated in October 2026 on a rental month counted from the delivery anniversary. Please check the dates — and whether a break of exactly the 60 days plus the rest of the month restarts the rental, or picks it up

rows.q: **Resources** — Chapter 10 has no resource list. Are there documents, forms or links CSRs should have?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to Billing?

**For:** Denials — **Monil Shah**, with **Bhoj Bhatt** (Billing Manager, the Denials backup)

rows.says: **Two calls go straight to the Denials team member working the case** — insurance responding to a Denials request, and a patient calling about a Denials invoice or the billing status while the case is open. Otherwise, the Denials Q (ext 101)
**The Denials row in the directory** — Monil Shah, backed up by Bhoj Bhatt; Denials members take direct transfers. Please check the holder, backup and how CSRs should reach your team
**The Claim Prep tab** — what "paid" and "eligible" mean, and the RR and NU modifiers
**Denials and appeals:** the common denial reasons, the 120-day redetermination window, and what a CSR tells the patient
**Prior authorizations** are submitted by the intake team's authorization members

rows.q: **What do you wish a CSR had already collected before transferring a call to Denials?**
**Anything else?** Is there anything in Denials' process a CSR should know that the manual lacks?
